doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Conducting for Ethel Merman; Cloris Leachman singing
summary: Dick Perry's advice about Merman, and a memory of Cloris Leachman struggling to start a song.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Did I tell you about what Dick Perry told me about Ethel Merman? I had to conduct for her one night. She had this great long medley. I mean a medley of everything she’d ever done kind of you know, from stem to stern? And I was frettin’ about it, to remember tempos. And Dick Perry said, he was one of the trumpet players—
He was one of the trumpet players in the Tonight Show band in New York, was Dick Perry.
Yeah. And he’d worked in the pit behind her on Broadway. He says, “Don’t worry.” He says, “when Ethel starts you go, and when she stops it’s over.”
Isn’t that nice to be in that position? Oh. I have one personal memory of the Tonight Show that I had to ask about. I think it was Cloris Leachman, and she thought she could sing or something.
And I remember the piano player, and it was probably you trying to help her find her note and it was like Ding [sings].
And she couldn’t get started. I felt so— and I’m thinking of you. Like how unsubtle are you going to get here. You know DING—
You help them out any way you can.
Well sad to say all actors think they can sing. Not many can.
